title: Migration & Retention Microdeck - Sandbox Draft
summary: A short, portable microdeck to help sellers run technical migration pilots while maximizing retention after model or deployment changes. Focused on quick win metrics, risk mitigations, and negotiation levers (pricing/credits/SLA). This is a sandbox draft for rapid iteration with SEs and a couple of pilot customers.
audience: AE/SE pairs running 2–6 week pilots with platform teams and product engineering managers at mid-market/enterprise accounts.
core_message: Frame the change as: low operational risk + measurable unit-cost improvement + reversible rollout lanes. Sell migration as a small, observable experiment with guardrails, not a big bang cutover.
use_cases: Replace hosted inference with Dedicated capacity to reduce per-token spend for high-throughput batch jobs
Swap in a quantized variant for embedding-heavy pipelines to cut cost without visible quality drop for retrieval tasks
Migrate from third-party managed endpoints to Redwood Private (VPC) for data residency/compliance while keeping production latency SLOs
success_metrics_for_trial: P50 latency change <= +20ms and P95 <= +50ms for representative routes
Token cost reduction >= 20% for the targeted workload after batching and KV-cache enabled
Regression rate on eval prompt-set <= 1.5% (defined by customer QA prompts)
seller_play_actions: Prep: request 72-hour synthetic trace and representative sample prompts from customer
One-week sandbox: deploy model variant behind canary routing 5-10% traffic, log metrics to Redwood Console
Two-week pilot: ramp to 25-50% with rolling rollback policy; execute scripted customer QA checks at each step
Close: package findings (latency, cost, quality) into a single-page exec summary; propose commit or reserved capacity options
pricing_and_incentives: Offer 'pilot credits' covering first 30 days of additional infra spend (typically 2–4k) to remove friction
Temporary blended pricing for first 3 months on Dedicated to smooth over initial unit-cost variability
Include a short-term SLA addendum for pilot phase: 99.5% uptime windowed to test routes
common_customer_objections: We can’t risk latency regressions — Response: use canary routing + exact-match replay of production traces; set P95 guardrail and automatic rollback
We already built an internal serving infra — Response: show TCO comparison for next 12 months including ops headcount and platform improvements
Security/regulatory controls block external pilots — Response: propose Redwood Private sandbox in their VPC or on-prem test box with KMS integration
demo_script: 1) Quick architecture slide (30s) — show how canary routing works. 2) Live Console: show token-level cost waterfall for baseline vs pilot (2m). 3) Traces: open a P95 latency trace and show KV-cache effect (90s). 4) Rollback demo: flip canary back to baseline and confirm metrics revert (60s). 5) Close with next-steps checklist and proposed credits (30s).
slide_outlines: Title: Migration & Retention Microdeck — elevator pitch + expected outcomes
Why change now: short bullets on cost pressure, model churn, compliance drivers
Pilot design: canary, metrics, rollback — diagram + step timeline
What we measure: latency, cost-per-token, quality (eval set), infra ops effort
Seller playbook: 7 tactical steps the AE/SE pair runs during trial
Incentives: pilot credits, blended pricing, short SLA addendum
Customer Qs & rebuttals: top 6 objections with proven responses
Case example (anonymized): pilot data showing 28% cost drop, negligible quality drift
Next steps and legal/finance checklist for converting to committed capacity
field_notes_and_tips: Always capture customer 'anchor' prompts — these are the minimum eval set we take across pilots
When asked about model parity, lean on quantitative regression gates rather than vague assurances
If the customer has bursty nightly workloads, propose time-windowed batching policy demos to show immediate wins
Keep the demo data load tiny — customers lose trust when demos are flaky; synthetic traces that mirror production are fine
checklist_for_pilot_kickoff: Agree on 3 metric thresholds (latency, cost, quality) and rollback triggers
Set up a shared Slack channel with ops contact and SE
Schedule mid-pilot check-in at day 7 and post-pilot review at day 21
Finance: confirm pilot credits and billing treatment for overages
open_questions_for-product: Can we automate a short-run billing report that isolates pilot traffic for the first 30 days?
Is there an easy toggle to enable KV-cache simulation mode in the sandbox to show benefits pre-deploy?
What standard legal language can we include for pilot SLAs to avoid lengthy contracts?
next_steps_for-this-draft: Share with two field AE/SE pairs this week, incorporate feedback from CONF-RT-2124, and produce a slide-ready version by 2025-02-10. Mark as in_review after first round of field edits.
notes_to_self: Keep this microdeck narrow — it’s intentionally tactical. If customers ask about long-term architecture, hand off to platform-seller playbook (separate doc).
